title: A product of geometrically irreducible schemes is geometrically irreducible
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] which are geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then the fibre product $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product], a scheme over $k$ through either projection followed by the structure morphism, is geometrically irreducible over $k$: for every field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] the base change $(X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 038F (lemma-bijection-irreducible-components), applied after base change to k' together with Tag 054P (lemma-geometrically-irreducible-check-after-extension); used in pic.tex Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): 'the product X^d is irreducible'

proof.text: Fix a field extension $k'/k$. By [lem-pc-base-change-product], the base change $(X\times_kY)\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is canonically the fibre product $X_{k'}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}Y_{k'}$ of the two base-changed schemes.

source.place: Tag 054P, the canonical identification of a base change of a fibre product with the fibre product of base changes

proof.text: The hypotheses that $X$ and $Y$ are geometrically irreducible over $k$ mean that $X_{k'}$ and $Y_{k'}$ are geometrically irreducible over $k'$: after any further field extension $K/k'$, their base changes $(X_{k'})\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $(Y_{k'})\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}\operatorname{Spec}K$ are identified by [def-pc-base-change] (the identification $X_{T'}\cong X_T\times_TT'$ for $T'=\operatorname{Spec}K\to T=\operatorname{Spec}k'$ over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$) with the base changes $X_K$ and $Y_K$ of $X$ and $Y$ along $K/k$, which are irreducible by hypothesis; irreducibility passes along these isomorphisms.

Apply [lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field] over the field $k'$ to the geometrically irreducible schemes $X_{k'}$ and $Y_{k'}$. It follows that $X_{k'}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}Y_{k'}$ is irreducible, and therefore, by the canonical isomorphism in Step 1, $(X\times_kY)\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is irreducible.
